items.title: Freeze Warning Issued For Lake Of The Ozarks Friday Night
items.desc: LAKE OF THE OZARKS, Mo. — Residents may want to protect plants and outdoor plumbing Friday night as the first widespread freeze of the season settles into central Missouri.
items.body: LAKE OF THE OZARKS, Mo. — Residents may want to protect plants and outdoor plumbing Friday night as the first widespread freeze of the season settles into central Missouri. The National Weather Service has issued a Freeze Warning for Camden, Miller, and Morgan counties from midnight Friday through 8 a.m. Saturday. The warning also covers several surrounding counties across central and southern Missouri. Temperatures are expected to fall into the upper 20s and lower 30s across the area, including Camdenton, Osage Beach, Lake Ozark, Eldon, Versailles, Laurie, and the Village of Four Seasons. The NWS says frost and freezing temperatures could kill sensitive plants and crops, and may damage unprotected outdoor plumbing. After a chilly start to the weekend, temperatures will warm to around 70 by Monday, with overnight lows generally in the 40s next week.

items.title: Ozark Law Is Back! Season 3 Premieres Tonight With More Lake Of The Ozarks Action
items.desc: A new season of Ozark Law premieres tonight at 8 p.m. Central on A&E, bringing viewers back to Lake of the Ozarks, where days on the water and late nights can turn into bad decisions.
items.body: A new season of Ozark Law premieres tonight at 8 p.m. Central on A&E, bringing viewers back to Lake of the Ozarks, where days on the water and late nights can turn into bad decisions. The documentary series returns for its third season on Nov. 4, following officers in Lake Ozark, Osage Beach, and Sunrise Beach as the small departments handle a surge in calls from the influx of summer tourists. This season looks especially busy as America celebrates its 250th birthday. From drug busts and unruly crowds on the Strip to officers chasing a black bear, the series follows local law enforcement as they work to keep the peace. If the season premiere leaves you wanting more, the previous 22 episodes are also available to watch. For most of the year, Missouri’s Lake of the Ozarks is a quiet haven of small towns and a few thousand residents but every summer, millions of tourists flood in for all-day fun on the water and rowdy nights at the bars. The influx of visitors turns this quiet oasis into a ‘round-the-clock job for the police. Following the small forces in Lake Ozark, Osage Beach and Sunrise Beach, “Ozark Law” spotlights what it takes to protect the peace in this midwestern paradise as well as the people who come to party. items.title: Leaf The Lake Alone! Ameren Warns Against Dumping Fall Leaves Into Lake Of The Ozarks
items.desc: Fall leaves may look harmless, but piles of them pushed into Lake of the Ozarks can create real problems for water quality.
items.body: Fall leaves may look harmless, but piles of them pushed into Lake of the Ozarks can create real problems for water quality. Residents, property owners, and lawn crews are being encouraged not to blow, dump, or push leaves and other yard waste into the Lake. Instead, Ameren Missouri recommends mulching, composting, or using an approved disposal service. Leaves that fall naturally into the Lake are part of its ecosystem. Problems can arise, however, when concentrated piles are intentionally pushed into the water. As that material decomposes, it can release nutrients, contribute to algae growth, and use oxygen needed by fish and other aquatic life. "When leaves are blown into a cove, they don't just disappear," said Bryan Vance, manager of shoreline management at Ameren Missouri. "As those leaves break down, they can affect water quality and create issues along the shoreline. Taking a few extra minutes to mulch, compost or properly dispose of leaves can make a real difference." - Mulch leaves. Run over leaves with a mower and use them around trees, shrubs, and garden beds to help retain moisture and suppress weeds. - Start or add to a compost pile. Combine leaves with grass clippings and food scraps to create nutrient-rich compost. - Bag and dispose of leaves properly. Check with local waste services, municipalities or landscaping companies for collection and composting options. If you hire a lawn service, ask how it disposes of collected leaves. Commercial landscaping and lawn care companies are prohibited from disposing of leaves and other yard waste in Missouri's public waters. - Burn only where permitted. items.title: Turbulence At City Hall: Who Will Run The Camdenton Airport?
items.desc: CAMDENTON, Mo. — The battle for control over the Camdenton airport continues, and elected officials and city staff are taking sides.
items.body: CAMDENTON, Mo. — The battle for control over the Camdenton airport continues, and elected officials and city staff are taking sides. The City has been considering bringing management of the airport in-house, after contracting with Lake Aviation Center for nearly two decades. The City Board of Aldermen was split 3-3 in a vote over the issue on Tuesday, Sept. 1. The motion on the table was to continue contracting Lake Aviation Services. Aldermen Don Neuharth, Daniel Ousley and Eric Faes voted in favor. Aldermen Brenda Weir, Sandy Gentry and Mark Anderson voted against. With the board deadlocked, Mayor John McNabb broke the tie by voting against the motion. At that meeting there were multiple citizens that questioned whether the city had employees with the specialized aviation experience and training required. They also praised Lake Aviation Center's Corey Leuwerke, who has managed the airport for 19 years. They credited Leuwerke's aviation knowledge, work ethic, ability to obtain grants and industry contacts with contributing to the airport's growth and success. But Camdenton City Administrator Jeff Hooker said the reason for bringing airport operations under city management was financial. According to Hooker, the city has been supplementing work at the airport annually through another city department's budget while not receiving most of the profits generated by airport operations. “The city needs to run the airport to assume the profits for the purpose of being self-sustaining,” Hooker stated. Under city management, revenue generated through airport operations could be used to offset the costs of operating and maintaining the facility. items.title: The Shroud Of Turin: Free Lake Area Exhibit Explores Its History & Mysteries
items.desc: LAURIE, Mo. — A traveling exhibit exploring the history, science, and religious significance of the Shroud of Turin is coming to the National Shrine of Mary, Mother of the Church, in Laurie this month.
items.body: LAURIE, Mo. — A traveling exhibit exploring the history, science, and religious significance of the Shroud of Turin is coming to the National Shrine of Mary, Mother of the Church, in Laurie this month. “Who is the Man of the Shroud?” will feature a replica of the Shroud of Turin, along with interpretive panels examining the cloth’s documented history, physical characteristics, scientific study, and connections to Gospel accounts of the Passion and burial of Jesus. The exhibit, being displayed Nov. 5-15, is presented by Shroud Exhibitors of Central Missouri in partnership with Othonia, Inc. Visitors will also be able to scan QR codes for an audio guide, quick facts, and additional educational resources. “We are truly excited to welcome the Shroud of Turin exhibit to the National Shrine of Mary, Mother of the Church,” said Andrew Wright, executive director of the Shrine. “The Shroud invites us to reflect on Christ’s suffering and sacrifice, the depth of His love for humanity, and the hope of His Resurrection.” The exhibit is intended for visitors of all ages and faith backgrounds and will be available free of charge, with donations encouraged to support Shroud Exhibitors of Central Missouri. The National Shrine of Mary, Mother of the Church is located at 176 Marian Drive in Laurie. The Shrine, also known as the Mothers’ Shrine, serves as a place for prayer, pilgrimage, and reflection and includes the Mothers’ Wall of Life and a large sculpture of Mary. - Wednesday through Friday: 10 a.m.–1 p.m. Visitors are encouraged to check mothersshrine.com or the Shrine’s Facebook page for current hours and additional information.

items.title: Needles In Halloween Candy? Sheriff Offers Free X-Rays After Lake Area Woman Says She Found Some
items.desc: CAMDEN COUNTY, Mo. — The Camden County Sheriff's Office is offering free X-Rays of kids' Halloween candy, after receiving a report from a local woman who said needles were found in her grandkids' treats.
items.body: CAMDEN COUNTY, Mo. — The Camden County Sheriff's Office is offering free X-Rays of kids' Halloween candy, after receiving a report from a local woman who said needles were found in her grandkids' treats. ATTENTION: Last night, Halloween, deputies took a confirmed report of a family finding needles in a piece of Halloween candy. This family was trick-or-treating in the HH area of Camden County. While the investigation into the source of the candy continues we would like to invite anyone concerned about the safety of their Halloween candy to bring it to the Camden County Justice Center for an X-ray. While the Justice Center is closed on Sundays we are opening the doors today from 11:00am to 2:00pm for anyone who wants to bring their candy in for inspection. We will also make this service available throughout this week during regular business hours. We have no information indicating this is anything more than an isolated incident but, out of an abundance of caution, we encourage anyone concerned to come to the Justice Center. The woman who made the report — a local schoolteacher named Sarah Stoufer — said her grandchildren had been trick-or-treating in the neighborhood on Palmer Road off Route HH, an extremely popular trick-or-treating location annually at the Lake. The sheriff's office says it was still investigating the source of the candy, but offered free X-Rays this week for anyone who wanted their children's candy checked. On Halloween night, the Hickory County, Missouri sheriff's office also announced they received a report of a Payday candy bar with a straight-pin inside it.

Free Alpha-Gal Testing Event Planned in Webster County
items.desc: Webster County residents can receive free alpha-gal testing and learn more about tick-borne diseases at an upcoming event in Fordland. Fordland Clinic and the Webster County Health Unit are partnering […]
items.body: Webster County residents can receive free alpha-gal testing and learn more about tick-borne diseases at an upcoming event in Fordland. Fordland Clinic and the Webster County Health Unit are partnering to offer the event on Tuesday, Nov. 3, from 9 a.m. to 2 p.m. at Fordland Clinic, 1059 Barton Drive. No appointment is needed. Testing will be available on a first-come, first-served basis, and residents are encouraged to arrive early because supplies may be limited. Alpha-gal syndrome is a potentially serious allergic condition caused by bites from certain ticks, including the Lone Star tick, which is common in Missouri. The condition can trigger allergic reactions after eating red meat or consuming certain products made from mammals. Symptoms may include hives, swelling, stomach pain, nausea, and difficulty breathing. Reactions sometimes occur several hours after eating. “Tick bites are more than just an outdoor nuisance. In some cases, they can have lasting health consequences,” said Debby Carl, nurse practitioner at Fordland Clinic. Carl said the event will give residents an opportunity to learn about prevention and receive testing at no cost. Webster County Health Unit staff will also provide tick prevention information and distribute prevention kits. Health officials recommend using tick repellent, wearing protective clothing, and checking for ticks after spending time outdoors. Residents experiencing possible symptoms of alpha-gal syndrome or another tick-borne illness are encouraged to contact a healthcare provider. Fordland Clinic offers follow-up care and accepts most private insurance plans, Medicaid, and Medicare. A sliding fee scale is available for qualifying patients. The Nov. 3 testing event is free for Webster County residents, with no appointment required.

Marshfield residents came close to reaching their donation goal during the Oct. 15 community blood drive at the Marshfield Senior Center. The drive, held in partnership with Community Blood Center of the Ozarks (CBCO), collected 37 donations toward a goal of 40, reaching 93 percent of its target. Among the regular donors making a difference is Wayne Burnett, who has given blood an impressive 329 times. According to CBCO, one blood donation can help save up to three lives. That means Burnett’s lifetime donations have the potential to help as many as 987 people. Another familiar face behind Marshfield’s blood drives is Vickie Brooks, who has supported CBCO for more than 30 years.
